title: Google wins zoning approval for huge data center near Detroit airport
key_facts: Van Buren Township's Planning Commission voted 5-1 on Wednesday evening (14 Oct) to approve the final site plan for Google's data center, called Project Cannoli, in Wayne County, Michigan.
The site is 282 acres between I-94 and I-275; it is already zoned industrial, so the board had to approve projects that fit those rules.
Google will own and run it; developer Panattoni manages construction.
Officials agreed to a $125 million tax break; Google agreed to pay $15 million each to the county and the township.
Panattoni says site construction brings $2 billion in contracts to local businesses and the finished site will host 50 to 200 employees.
Neighbours complained of noise, dust and construction; trustees have faced recall efforts over their backing.
quote_evidence: After nearly an hour of public comment at a zoning board meeting on Wednesday evening, members of the Van Buren Township Planning Commission voted 5-1 to approve a final site plan for the project.
Our job as planning commissioners is to verify that the construction is in line with the law.
why_it_matters_hint: The vote was a legal formality, but it shows local anger over big data centers and the tax breaks that attract them.
notes: Quote on the commission's duty is from trustee Jeff Jahr.
